column10: normalized-expectation
Equivalent syntax tree, token spans, and diagnostics for valid and invalid modules.
Character indexes, inclusive/exclusive endpoints, movement, growth, containment, and adjacency agree.
JSON imports and resolved-import URIs parse into deterministic maps and sets.
Empty, stdlib, package, file, relative, service-provider, and editor transformers preserve order and URI substitutions.
Repeated close is safe, later use fails deterministically, and owned resources are released.
Preconfigured and unconfigured builders retain setters/getters, reject invalid combinations, and build independent evaluators.
Module factories, resolved keys, paths, resources, and readers expose useful factories, metadata, nullable misses, bytes, and explicit ownership.
HTTP clients and proxy rules expose byte certificates, request and stream helpers, deterministic failures, and repeat-safe disposal.
Package URIs, assets, checksums, dependencies, metadata streams, resolvers, and caches expose their consumer-facing contracts.
Projects, dependencies, evaluator settings, user settings, HTTP configuration, and external-reader configuration retain resolved values and invalid-input failures.
Security builders expose immutable policy views, remain fail closed, and external-reader startup and shutdown preserve explicit process ownership.
Public loading APIs expose Uri, Stream, byte arrays, nullable returns, read-only collections, .NET exceptions, and IDisposable boundaries.
Constructors, named/settable members, attributes, required members, unknown properties, and cycles bind or fail deterministically.
Nested collection, pair, map, nullable, and generic metadata recursively controls conversion.
Identity, numeric, URI/path, regex, duration, version, collection, and custom conversions preserve success and failure behavior.
Evaluator ownership, binder reuse, generic evaluation, expressions, and disposal are explicit.
Modules, classes, aliases, imports, docs, annotations, nullable/constrained types, and deterministic ordering generate compilable C#.
Owned type parameters and constraints map to compilable C# generics while unsupported user-defined generic declarations fail stably.
Abstract/open bases, overrides, imported derived values, and runtime class identity survive generation and binding.
